bullets.text: Goal: lock the new pricing page structure so Leah can start high-fidelity designs this week.
The page gets ~18,000 visits/month with 2.1% visit-to-trial conversion, against a 3–4% B2B analytics benchmark.
Session recordings show visitors bouncing between Growth and Enterprise, with ~3 minutes on page that reads as confusion.
Leah reviewed ~40 recordings: visitors click contact sales and then abandon the 9-field form.
Arjun estimated the fully loaded cost at ~$3 per million events, so $25/M overage keeps a healthy margin and sits mid-market vs Mixpanel/Amplitude.
Annual uptake on Growth is already 61%.
Showing an Enterprise price could anchor deals low; the median Enterprise deal is ~$42k/yr.
Overage is handled manually today; sales spent ~60 hours last month on overage conversations.
The November 3 launch is tight given ~2 sprints of Stripe metered billing work.
Listing AI Insights under a tier before packaging is decided could anger customers.
Ship 'what drives price' copy for Enterprise with no number, A/B tested against a 'starting at' price over ~6 weeks.
Growth overage at $25 per additional million events, with an on-page calculator capped at 50M.
Keep the 20% annual discount; revisit in Q1 after the Enterprise test.
Contact form cut from 9 fields to 5 (one optional free-text field).
AI Insights stays off the page except a teaser banner until Q4 roadmap planning settles packaging.
Leah: high-fidelity designs incl. the calculator by next Wednesday, early Figma link Monday.
Sofia: experiment brief by Friday, plus billing work with Aman.
James: sales playbook and lead routing updated by the 20th, with a walkthrough at the Monday sales sync.
Tom: pricing change announcement for existing Growth customers; launch target November 3.
Lock the structure of the new pricing page: Enterprise pricing, usage-based overage, annual discount, form and comparison table.
Whether to show a starting price for Enterprise, with Sofia for it and James against.
Pay-as-you-go overage on Growth and a slider calculator.
Cutting the annual discount from 20% to 15–17%, with the churn data debated.
Collapsing the 42-row comparison table to 8 key rows.
Where the team disagrees on pricing, tests settle it, one test at a time.
Annual Growth logos churn ~1.2%/mo vs ~3.4%/mo for monthly, though Sofia notes that may be correlation.
Sofia believes keeping 20% leaves roughly $40k/yr on the table.
Designs by next Wednesday, experiment brief Friday, playbook by the 20th, launch November 3.
Check the launch date again next Thursday in case billing slips.
